basics.name: Ruşen Birben
basics.summary: AI and Data Engineering graduate from Istanbul Technical University and independent researcher with METU’s Applied NLP Group. Research interests center on LLM robustness and reliability, with experience in Turkish NLP, machine unlearning, and LLM applications for finance.
basics.printSummary: AI and Data Engineering graduate from Istanbul Technical University and independent researcher with METU’s Applied NLP Group. Research interests center on LLM robustness and reliability, with experience in Turkish NLP, machine unlearning, and LLM applications for finance.

experience.description: Contribute to data creation and evaluation methodology for the SIGTURK 2027 benchmark on Turkic languages and cultural understanding with Çağrı Toraman. Support LlamaTurk2 through training-data collection and pretraining experiments. Also lead [METU NLP Connect](https://www.youtube.com/@metunlpconnect), producing expert interviews.

Co-founded Fiction Studios with a friend at Bilkent Cyberpark and served as technical lead. Directed technical development and coordinated three additional contributors supporting the two founders. Built a multilingual LLM-powered guide for museums and tourists, working on the conversational visitor experience alongside customer and investor discussions.

Joined CyberQuote, a Phillip Capital subsidiary, as the second member of its newly formed AI team. Developed news-sentiment pipelines and internal LLM tools for financial professionals, alongside web integrations and a mobile voice assistant. Worked with the practical challenge of retrieving current financial context from fragmented sources and PDF reports, where missing information could lead to unreliable answers.
Investigated software-log analysis for predictive maintenance and developed prototypes using HDFS logs.

Researched LLM applications in finance, including sentiment analysis, tool use, reasoning, forecasting, and retrieval-augmented generation. Conducted part of the experiments that contributed to Kaira, my undergraduate capstone on financial reasoning with LLMs.

projects.title: Kaira
projects.subtitle: Undergraduate Capstone: Financial Reasoning LLM
projects.description: Explored financial reasoning in Qwen-based LLMs through GRPO fine-tuning with Unsloth and LoRA. Ran FinQA and GSM8K experiments to examine reward design and reasoning behavior, and developed an Ollama-based chat application. Undergraduate capstone at Istanbul Technical University.

projects.title: AIZheimer
projects.subtitle: Machine Unlearning in Stable Diffusion
projects.description: Building on Forget-Me-Not, implemented and adapted cross-attention-based unlearning for Stable Diffusion 2.1. Developed attention controller/processor code and explored attention re-steering, distraction, and random-stimulus loss objectives. Ran qualitative experiments and prepared visualizations to examine the trade-off between removing a target concept and retaining unrelated generation capabilities.

projects.title: Biting The Bytes
projects.subtitle: Turkish Diacritic Restoration
projects.description: Fine-tuned ByT5-small with PEFT/LoRA for Turkish diacritic restoration, treating the task as byte-level token classification. Took primary responsibility for model training and hyperparameter tuning; shared debugging and Hugging Face Spaces deployment with a teammate. The project explored restoring characters such as ş, ç, ı, ğ, ü, and ö in noisy or ASCII-only Turkish text.

projects.title: To-AI-or-Not-to-AI
projects.subtitle: GPT Detector
projects.description: Fine-tuned three RoBERTa-based detectors and combined their predictions through majority voting. Shared data creation and preprocessing for a 26,270-example dataset, and deployed the application on Hugging Face Spaces. The ensemble achieved 94.21% accuracy on an in-domain random test split; this evaluation did not establish performance across languages or substantially different domains.

projects.title: Tobor
projects.subtitle: Autonomous Warehouse Robot
projects.description: Contributed to a team-built autonomous warehouse robot combining navigation and YOLO-based perception in ROS2. Implemented the box pickup and drop-off mechanism, shared data annotation with the team, and supported work on other algorithms.
